paths.description: Public company detail and financial-data archetype

findings.summary: The default theme ignores the system dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is byte-identical to the normal desktop capture, and the rendered body is hard-coded class="light" despite dark-aware theme-color metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Make Auto the initial theme, declare color-scheme: light dark, and resolve surfaces and controls through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(); retain explicit Light/Dark overrides.

findings.summary: Route and substantial state changes use abrupt swaps rather than View Transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection across home, listing, and company routes found no view-transition declarations, while navigation changes the full document.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively add same-document transitions for modal/state changes and cross-document view transitions for stable shared elements, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is driven only by viewport media queries, not component containers.
findings.evidence: The company probe found zero container-query rules; listing DOM shows reused cards switch only at global min-width breakpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish container-type on reusable card/list regions and move local layout switches to @container rules, retaining viewport rules only for page-level composition.

findings.summary: The core company-detail template misses the good LCP threshold in Lighthouse.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 3.3s and FCP 2.7s on the company page, although CLS was 0 and TBT only 20ms. The independent trace was faster at 1.80s, indicating variable but real load latency.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element, reduce document/font critical-path latency, preload only the required font face, and prioritize the actual LCP resource while deferring noncritical chart/analytics work.

findings.summary: Fonts and five parser-blocking stylesheets dominate the initial network budget.
findings.evidence: The HAR reports 570KB transferred; three fonts account for 349KB (61%), including a 228KB variable font, and five VeryHigh-priority parser-inserted stylesheets precede content.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset and split fonts by used weight/script, use an effective font-display strategy and stable fallback metrics, consolidate or defer noncritical CSS, and preload only the font required above the fold.

findings.summary: The company template ships avoidable chart-library JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 28,521 unused bytes in the 68,494-byte Chart.js bundle, 41.6% of that resource.
findings.suggestedFix: Load chart code on demand when the chart approaches the viewport, and build/import only the controllers, scales, and plugins used by this page.

findings.summary: Important company navigation and financial values fail WCAG text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.44:1 for #808c95 navigation and values on white, 3.47:1 for the red daily change, and additional chart controls below 4.5:1. The company accessibility score was 0.88.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken muted ink, negative-value red, and active-control colors until normal text reaches at least 4.5:1 in every theme; preserve non-color state cues.

findings.summary: The public homepage has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe returned metaDescription:null and Lighthouse failed the meta-description audit, despite a descriptive title.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, page-specific meta description describing Indian stock screening and fundamental analysis.

findings.summary: Public templates do not expose canonical URLs.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no rel=canonical on the homepage or sampled company page. Robots permits these routes and the sitemap includes public templates, so canonical consolidation is appropriate.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit an absolute self-referencing canonical on each indexable template and normalize consolidated/query variants to the intended canonical URL.

findings.summary: Entity pages lack structured data and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found zero JSON-LD and Open Graph tags, and company DOM inspection found a meta description but no JSON-LD, Open Graph, or canonical metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite metadata globally and entity-appropriate JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter preview tags on company and screen pages, matching visible content.

findings.summary: The CSP permits unsafe inline script and broad HTTPS script sources; Permissions-Policy is absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found script-src with unsafe-inline and scheme-wide https:, while Permissions-Policy was missing. HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, and Referrer-Policy were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Move inline handlers/scripts to nonce- or hash-authorized files, narrow script-src to required origins (optionally strict-dynamic), and add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Account creation offers password and federated login but no passkey path.
findings.evidence: The registration DOM exposes a required password field and Google sign-in, with no WebAuthn/passkey registration affordance or navigator.credentials use in the sampled flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey creation and authentication as the preferred phishing-resistant path, keeping federated/password recovery as proportionate fallbacks.

findings.evidence: The form probe found empty autocomplete values on email, repeated email, and password fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete="email" on the email field and autocomplete="new-password" on account-creation password fields; reconsider requiring a duplicated email entry.

findings.summary: Font and analytics resources are disproportionate for a mostly text-and-table page.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributes 349KB to fonts and 31.6KB to two analytics systems (Plausible and Rybbit); font bytes are the largest share of the 570KB transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset fonts and defer optional faces; review whether two analytics clients are necessary, and load/batch measurement after core content without extending session-wide work.

findings.summary: The app is installable but provides no offline fallback.
findings.evidence: A manifest and active service worker are present, but the fetched service worker defines push/notification handlers only; its fetch handler is commented out and there is no cache or offline response.
findings.suggestedFix: Precache a small offline document and essential shell assets, then handle navigation failures with a clear offline/retry state while keeping live financial data explicitly marked unavailable or stale.
